name: Onion
grown_as: The bulb onion, a biennial grown as an annual from sets (small bulbs) for its single round bulb. William has 'Autumn Champion' and 'Red Winter' (red skin, blue-green leaves). Drawn with golden-brown skin. ⚠️ CHECK: should the drawing be golden or red?
habit: Year 1: a fan of 6 to 10 upright hollow leaves 30 to 50 cm from a single round bulb that swells at the soil surface. Year 2: one or more tall, hollow flower stems 60 to 120 cm, swollen like a long balloon below the middle, each with a round head.

leaf.arrangement: In two ranks from the neck of the bulb, wrapping one inside the next
leaf.outline: Long, hollow, round to half-round tube, 30 to 50 cm by 1 to 2 cm, a little flattened on the upper side

flower.form: A round ball of many small star-shaped flowers
flower.petals: Six tepals, free, oval, spreading into a small star
flower.colour: Greenish-white to white, each tepal with a green midstripe
flower.centre: Six stamens sticking out well beyond the tepals, with green-yellow anthers; a green ovary
flower.behind: A papery spathe of two or three short lobes, splitting and folding back under the head
flower.carried: Hundreds of flowers on thin stalks from one point, in a dense round umbel at the top of a tall hollow stem that is swollen below the middle
flower.size: Flowers 4 to 6 mm; heads 4 to 8 cm across
flower.season: June to August of the second year

fruit: A dry round head of three-lobed capsules that split to show black, angular, wrinkled seeds.
seedling: Not drawn as a seedling: grown from sets. (From seed: one thin seed leaf bent like a hairpin, as in leek.)
winter: Bulbs are lifted and dried in summer and stored. Autumn-planted sets overwinter as a few thin upright leaves.

leaf: a long hollow round tube, not flat
smooth waxy blue-green with no teeth
bloom: a round ball of many small greenish-white star-shaped flowers
a papery spathe folded back below
set: a small onion bulb 1 to 2 cm with golden papery skin
a pointed neck and a flat root plate
young: a few upright hollow blue-green leaves from a small bulb at the soil
crop: a round bulb with golden-brown papery skin sitting half on top of the soil
leaves yellowing and fallen over at the neck
a tuft of white roots below
flower: a tall hollow flower stem swollen below the middle
a round greenish-white head on top
seedhead: a dry round head of papery capsules with black seeds

look_alikes: Shallot is the same species making a cluster of smaller bulbs. Leek and garlic have flat solid leaves. Welsh onion (Allium fistulosum) has hollow leaves but little or no bulb. Chives have much thinner leaves and pink-purple heads.
